# Kition Tessera

> The design system for professional editors and Kition kits: design tokens (`@kition/tessera-tokens`), Tessera Icons (`@kition/tessera-icons`), and components (`@kition/tessera`). A kit editor imports all of it through `@kition/kit-ui`.

## Overview

Getting started. Kition Tessera is the design system for professional editors: design tokens, Tessera Icons, and the components kits are built from.

### Three packages

`@kition/tessera-tokens`: the Kit Harness Protocol theme tokens (`--kit-*`), component tokens, and skins (Paper, Graphite) as CSS variables, TypeScript, and Rust.

`@kition/tessera-icons`: every icon as SVG path data on a 24 grid, as React components (`LayersIcon`), canvas drawing (`drawIcon`), SVG markup (`toSvg`), and the Rust crate `tessera-icons` for engines.

`@kition/tessera`: the components on these pages. They draw only through the theme tokens, so a host restyles all of them by sending one theme.

```tsx
import '@kition/tessera/styles.css'
import { Button, ColorPicker } from '@kition/tessera'
import { LayersIcon } from '@kition/tessera-icons/react'
```

### Principles

Built for professional software: ribbons, docks, colour wheels, curves, timelines and meters sit beside buttons and fields.

Styled only by tokens: no component hard-codes a colour, radius or shadow; skins and hosts change them all.

One icon family: a 24 grid, a 1.5 stroke, round caps; tool icons carry accents in the skin colour.

Accessible by default: labels, keyboard use, focus rings, and every skin held to WCAG AA contrast.

## Using Tessera in a kit

Getting started. How a Kition kit editor uses Tessera: everything arrives through @kition/kit-ui, under the names kits already use.

### Import from kit-ui

A kit editor depends on `@kition/kit-ui` only. kit-ui re-exports every Tessera component under its usual name, wires them to the Kit UI protocol (the host’s theme, locale, hidden and disabled elements, host buttons), and loads Tessera’s stylesheet from its own.

Icons come from `@kition/tessera-icons/react` when the kit lists it in package.json, or from kit-ui’s `TesseraIcons` namespace otherwise. Bundlers keep only the icons a kit uses.

```tsx
import '@kition/kit-ui/styles.css'
import { Button, RibbonGroup, RibbonButton, NumberField, TesseraIcons } from '@kition/kit-ui'
import { LayersIcon } from '@kition/tessera-icons/react' // or TesseraIcons.LayersIcon
```

### Icons for engine commands

Ribbons and menus built from engine commands get their icons from kit-ui’s rules: a command’s verb first (`edit.undo`, `layer.mergeDown`), then what it acts on, then the neutral command mark.

A kit names icons for the commands the rules cannot read in `web/src/commandIcons.ts`, imported once from `main.tsx`.

```tsx
import { registerCommandIcons } from '@kition/kit-ui'
import { DimensionAlignedIcon, FilletIcon } from '@kition/tessera-icons/react'

registerCommandIcons({
  dimaligned: DimensionAlignedIcon,
  fillet: FilletIcon,
})
```

### Rules for kits

Draw every colour, radius and shadow from the theme tokens (`var(--kit-*)`), never literal values, so skins reach your editor.

Pass icon sizes and `strokeWidth={ICON_STROKE}` from kit-ui; never a number of your own.

New icons go into Tessera (`packages/icons/svg/`, docs/icon-style.md), not into the kit.

Give elements a Kit UI id (`uiId`, `RibbonGroup id`) so hosts can hide or disable them.

### A new kit

kition-sdk’s `tools/new-kit-ui.mjs` scaffolds a kit editor on kit-ui and Tessera Icons, with its dev server allowed to read kition-tessera.

```tsx
node tools/new-kit-ui.mjs --repo ../kition-mykit --id kit.mykit --name MyKit --crate mykit --module kition_mykit_sdk --class MyKitDocument --sample sample.mykit --accept .mykit --port 5300
```

## Theming and skins

Getting started. A host sends one theme over the Kit Harness Protocol; every kit, and every Tessera component in it, follows.

### The theme

Hosts send `theme` in `ui/initialize` and `ui/theme`: a colour scheme and the 15 `--kit-*` theme tokens. kit-ui applies them to the document root; components read them through CSS variables.

`@kition/tessera-tokens` gives every skin’s theme ready to send (`SKINS.paper`, `SKINS.graphite`), and its tests hold each skin to WCAG AA.

```tsx
import { skinTheme } from '@kition/tessera-tokens'

kit.notify('ui/theme', { theme: skinTheme('graphite') })
```

### Proposal: KitTheme 2.0

KHP-0007 (draft) widens the theme to 35 tokens with fallbacks (chrome, panels, fields, overlays, accents), adds density and icon style, and defines a portable `skin.json`.

## Icons

Getting started. Tessera Icons: one family for interface and tool icons, in React, canvas, SVG, and Rust.

### Use

Browse and copy every icon on the Icons page. Tool icons (`family: "tool"`) carry accent areas filled with `--kit-icon-accent`; pass `accent={false}` for plain line.

```tsx
import { LayersIcon } from '@kition/tessera-icons/react'
import { Layers, drawIcon, toSvg } from '@kition/tessera-icons'

<LayersIcon size={16} />
drawIcon(ctx, Layers, 8, 8, { size: 16, color: '#5645d4' })
```

### Style

24 grid with a 20 live area, 1.5 round strokes, radius 2 corners, half-unit coordinates, 2-unit gaps; one metaphor per action. The full rules are in docs/icon-style.md; redraws are reviewed on the Redraw review page.

## Button

General. Starts an action. One primary button per view; the rest secondary or ghost.

```ts
import { Button, ButtonLink } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- The main action of a dialog or panel (primary).
- Other actions beside it (secondary, ghost).
- Destructive actions after a choice (danger).

When not to:

- Navigation to another page: use a link.
- Toolbar commands: use IconButton or a ribbon button.

### Example: Variants

Secondary is outlined; subtle is a quiet filled button; a disabled filled button turns muted, not faint.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  return (
    <div className="demo-row">
      <Button variant="primary" size="md">Save</Button>
      <Button variant="secondary" size="md">Cancel</Button>
      <Button variant="subtle" size="md">Duplicate</Button>
      <Button variant="ghost" size="md">More</Button>
      <Button variant="danger" size="md">Delete</Button>
      <Button variant="danger-outline" size="md">Disable</Button>
      <Button variant="primary" size="md" disabled>Disabled</Button>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Example: Sizes

Without a size the button keeps the 30px of editor chrome.

```tsx
import { Button } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  return (
    <div className="demo-row">
      <Button variant="primary" size="sm">Small (32)</Button>
      <Button variant="primary" size="md">Medium (36)</Button>
      <Button variant="primary" size="lg">Large (40)</Button>
      <Button>Editor chrome (30)</Button>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Example: Loading, icons, icon only

Icons inside a button draw at 16px; an icon-only button is square and needs an aria-label.

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button } from '@kition/tessera'
import { PlusIcon, SettingsIcon } from '@kition/tessera-icons/react'

export default function Demo() {
  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false)
  return (
    <div className="demo-row">
      <Button
        variant="primary"
        size="md"
        loading={saving}
        onClick={() => {
          setSaving(true)
          setTimeout(() => setSaving(false), 1500)
        }}
      >
        {saving ? 'Saving…' : 'Save'}
      </Button>
      <Button variant="secondary" size="md">
        <PlusIcon /> New record
      </Button>
      <Button variant="ghost" size="md" iconOnly aria-label="Settings">
        <SettingsIcon />
      </Button>
      <Button variant="secondary" size="sm" iconOnly aria-label="Add">
        <PlusIcon />
      </Button>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Example: Links drawn as buttons

```tsx
import { ButtonLink } from '@kition/tessera'
import { ArrowLeftIcon, MailIcon } from '@kition/tessera-icons/react'

export default function Demo() {
  return (
    <div className="demo-row">
      <ButtonLink variant="primary" size="md" href="#sign-in">
        Sign in again
      </ButtonLink>
      <ButtonLink size="md" href="#home">
        <ArrowLeftIcon size={16} />
        Back to the console
      </ButtonLink>
      <ButtonLink variant="ghost" size="md" href="mailto:hello@example.com">
        <MailIcon size={16} />
        Contact support
      </ButtonLink>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Button props

A button. Its `className` adds to Tessera's, so a host can adjust one button's layout.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `ButtonVariant` |  |  |
| `size` | `ControlSize` |  | Without `size` a button keeps the editor chrome's 30px. |
| `iconOnly` | `boolean` |  | A square button holding only an icon; give it an `aria-label`. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  | Shows a spinner before the label and marks the button busy, while its action runs. |

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

### ButtonLink props

A link that looks like a button: for navigation (another page, a sign-in URL, a mail link) drawn as an action.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant` | `ButtonVariant` |  |  |
| `size` | `ControlSize` |  |  |
| `render` | `(props: AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement> & { className: string; children?: ReactNode }) => ReactNode` |  | Draws the link another way: a router passes its own (`(props) => <Link to="/" {...props} />`). |

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

## Spinner

General. A spinning circle for work in progress.

```ts
import { Spinner } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- Inside a button while its action runs (Button `loading`).
- Next to a status that is still updating.

When not to:

- Long work with known progress: show the progress.

### Example: Sizes and a label

```tsx
import { Spinner } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  return (
    <div className="demo-row">
      <Spinner />
      <Spinner size={24} label="Loading the workspace" />
      <span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, color: 'var(--kit-text-muted)' }}>
        <Spinner size={14} /> Syncing…
      </span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Spinner props

A spinning circle for work in progress; `label` names it for screen readers (otherwise it is decorative).

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `number` | `16` |  |
| `label` | `string` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## IconButton

General. An icon-only button with an accessible label; `pressed` makes it a toggle.

```ts
import { IconButton } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- Toolbars, tool rails, panel headers.

When not to:

- An action whose icon is not obvious: use a Button with a label.

### Example: Toggles in a bar

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { IconButton } from '@kition/tessera'
import { BoldIcon, ItalicIcon, UnderlineIcon } from '@kition/tessera-icons/react'

export default function Demo() {
  const [bold, setBold] = useState(true)
  return (
    <div className="demo-row">
      <IconButton icon={BoldIcon} label="Bold" pressed={bold} onClick={() => setBold(!bold)} />
      <IconButton icon={ItalicIcon} label="Italic" />
      <IconButton icon={UnderlineIcon} label="Underline" disabled />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### IconButton props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `icon` (required) | `IconComponent` |  |  |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `pressed` | `boolean` |  |  |

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

## Badge

General. A small count or status beside a label.

```ts
import { Badge } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- The number of records in a view.
- A Beta or New mark.

When not to:

- An action: use a Button.

### Example: Count and status

```tsx
import { Badge } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  return (
    <div className="demo-row">
      <span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, fontSize: 14 }}>
        Grid view <Badge>128</Badge>
      </span>
      <span style={{ display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 8, fontSize: 14 }}>
        AI fields <Badge>Beta</Badge>
      </span>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Badge props

A small count or status beside a label (records in a view, a beta mark).

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

## Card

General. A product card: 12px radius, a hairline, a light shadow.

```ts
import { Card, CardHeader, CardContent } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- Grouping settings or a summary on a page.

### Example: Header and content

```tsx
import { Button, Card, CardContent, CardHeader } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  return (
    <Card style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
      <CardHeader>
        <strong>Model</strong>
        <Button size="sm">Change</Button>
      </CardHeader>
      <CardContent>Claude Opus · 1,240 credits this month</CardContent>
    </Card>
  )
}
```

### Card props

A product card: 12px radius, a hairline, a light shadow.

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

### CardHeader props

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

### CardContent props

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

## Disclosure

General. A section that opens and closes under its title.

```ts
import { Disclosure } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- Advanced settings most people do not need.

### Example: Closed and open

```tsx
import { Disclosure, TextInput } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  return (
    <div style={{ maxWidth: 360 }}>
      <Disclosure title="Advanced settings">
        <TextInput size="md" defaultValue="0.7" aria-label="Temperature" />
      </Disclosure>
      <Disclosure title="Usage" defaultOpen>
        1,240 credits this month
      </Disclosure>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Disclosure props

A section that opens and closes under its title.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `defaultOpen` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `open` | `boolean` |  | Open, when the screen holds the state (with `onOpenChange`). |
| `onOpenChange` | `(open: boolean) => void` |  |  |
| `onClose` | `() => void` |  | Called when the person closes it. |
| `children` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## TextInput

Forms. A single-line text field in three sizes: sm (toolbars), md (panels), lg (forms).

```ts
import { TextInput } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

### Example: Sizes and invalid

```tsx
import { TextInput } from '@kition/tessera'
import { SearchIcon } from '@kition/tessera-icons/react'

export default function Demo() {
  return (
    <div className="demo-stack">
      <TextInput placeholder="sm: kit toolbars (28)" />
      <TextInput size="md" placeholder="md: panels and settings (36)" />
      <TextInput size="lg" placeholder="lg: forms and dialogs (44)" />
      <TextInput size="md" defaultValue="not-an-email" invalid />
      <TextInput size="md" type="search" aria-label="Search users" placeholder="Search users" prefix={<SearchIcon size={16} />} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### TextInput props

A single-line text field. `invalid` marks it (and `aria-invalid`) after a failed check.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `ControlSize` | `'sm'` |  |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `prefix` | `ReactNode` |  | An icon (or short text) inside the field before the text: a search glass, a person. |
| `wrapperClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the box around the field and its prefix (layout: width, margins). |

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

## PasswordInput

Forms. A password field with a show and hide button outside the tab order.

```ts
import { PasswordInput } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

### Example: Show and hide

```tsx
import { PasswordInput } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  return <PasswordInput size="md" defaultValue="sk-test-not-a-real-key" aria-label="API key" />
}
```

### PasswordInput props

A password field with a show/hide button; the button keeps out of the tab order. `className`
goes on the field itself, as on TextInput.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `ControlSize` | `'sm'` |  |
| `prefix` | `ReactNode` |  | An icon (or short text) inside the field before the text: a search glass, a person. |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `wrapperClassName` | `string` |  | Classes for the box around the field and its show/hide button (layout: width, margins). |

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

## Textarea

Forms. Multi-line text.

```ts
import { Textarea } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

### Example: Prompt

```tsx
import { Textarea } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  return <Textarea rows={3} placeholder="Describe the change for the agent…" />
}
```

### Textarea props

Multi-line text.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  |  |

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

## Select

Forms. A drop-down: a native select drawn as Tessera’s control, for the platform’s popup and accessibility.

```ts
import { Select } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When not to:

- Two or three options always visible: use Segmented or Choice.

### Example: Sizes

```tsx
import { Select } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  return (
    <div className="demo-stack">
      <Select defaultValue="sheet" aria-label="Kit">
        <option value="sheet">Sheet</option>
        <option value="slide">Slide</option>
        <option value="photo">Photo</option>
      </Select>
      <Select size="lg" defaultValue="slide" aria-label="Kit (large)">
        <option value="sheet">Sheet</option>
        <option value="slide">Slide</option>
      </Select>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Select props

A drop-down. It stays a native select, as kits' do, for the platform's popup and accessibility,
drawn as Tessera's control. Children are `<option>`s.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `size` | `ControlSize` | `'sm'` |  |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  |  |

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

## Switch

Forms. An on/off switch for a setting that applies at once.

```ts
import { Switch } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- A setting that takes effect without a Save.

When not to:

- A choice saved with a form: use Checkbox.

### Example: On, off, disabled

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Switch } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  const [sync, setSync] = useState(true)
  return (
    <div className="demo-stack">
      <label style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 10, fontSize: 14 }}>
        <Switch checked={sync} onCheckedChange={setSync} aria-label="Sync across devices" /> Sync across devices: {sync ? 'on' : 'off'}
      </label>
      <label style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 10, fontSize: 14, color: 'var(--kit-text-muted)' }}>
        <Switch disabled aria-label="Beta features" /> Beta features (unavailable)
      </label>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Switch props

An on/off switch for a setting that applies at once. Controlled with `checked` and `onCheckedChange`.

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

## Field

Forms. A label, a control, and its hint or error, wired for screen readers.

```ts
import { Field } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- Every form control with a visible label.

### Example: Validation

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Field, TextInput } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  const [email, setEmail] = useState('not-an-email')
  const valid = /^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/.test(email)
  return (
    <Field label="Email" hint="We only use it to sign you in." error={valid ? undefined : 'Enter an email address.'}>
      {({ id, describedBy, invalid }) => (
        <TextInput id={id} aria-describedby={describedBy} invalid={invalid} size="md" value={email} onChange={(event) => setEmail(event.target.value)} />
      )}
    </Field>
  )
}
```

### Field props

A label, a control, and its help or error, wired together for screen readers.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `hint` | `ReactNode` |  | Help under the control; replaced by `error` when there is one. |
| `error` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode \| ((ids: { id: string; describedBy: string \| undefined; invalid: boolean }) => ReactNode)` |  | The control. Given a function, it receives the ids to put on it (`id`, `aria-describedby`). |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## NumberField

Forms. A number with a label you drag to scrub, arrows to step, and units.

```ts
import { NumberField } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- Opacity, size, angle, any bounded number in a panel.

### Example: Scrub, type, or arrow

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { NumberField } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  const [opacity, setOpacity] = useState(80)
  const [angle, setAngle] = useState(15)
  return (
    <div className="demo-stack">
      <NumberField label="Opacity" value={opacity} min={0} max={100} unit="%" onChange={(value) => setOpacity(value)} />
      <NumberField label="Angle" value={angle} min={-180} max={180} step={1} unit="°" onChange={(value) => setAngle(value)} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### NumberField props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `name` | `string` |  | The field's accessible name and tooltip when `label` is a symbol rather than words (Photoshop's Character panel labels its fields with glyphs: tT, A↕, VA); `label` by default. |
| `value` (required) | `number` |  |  |
| `min` (required) | `number` |  |  |
| `max` (required) | `number` |  |  |
| `step` | `number` |  | Step for arrows and scrubbing; decimals shown follow it (1 → integer). |
| `unit` | `string` |  |  |
| `onChange` (required) | `(value: number, final: boolean) => void` |  | Called while scrubbing with `final: false`, and once with `final: true` on release, Enter, or blur. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `width` | `number` |  |  |
| `testId` | `string` |  |  |
| `uiId` | `string` |  | A Kit UI id when the field is a declared element. |
| `track` | `boolean` |  | A slider row: the label and field on one line, a slider from `min` to `max` under them. |
| `hot` | `boolean` |  | Hot text (Premiere's, upstream Film's `widgets::hot_number`): the value and its unit drawn as accent text, without a box or a visible label (`label` names it). Dragged sideways it scrubs by `speed` per CSS pixel (Shift ten times faster, Cmd, Ctrl, or Alt ten times finer), reporting `final: false` per move and the last value again with `final: true` on release; a click opens a field to type into, which commits on Enter or blur and leaves unchanged on Escape. |
| `speed` | `number` |  | Hot text: value units per CSS pixel dragged (`step` by default). |
| `onDone` | `() => void` |  | Hot text: called once a typed edit ends (Enter, Escape, or blur), so the editor can take the focus back. |

## Bar controls

Forms. Compact controls for options bars: Segmented, Choice, Checkbox, Hint, BarSeparator.

```ts
import { Segmented, Choice, Checkbox, Hint, BarSeparator } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- A tool’s options above the canvas.

### Example: An options bar

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { BarSeparator, Checkbox, Choice, Hint, Segmented } from '@kition/tessera'
import { TextAlignCenterIcon, TextAlignEndIcon, TextAlignStartIcon } from '@kition/tessera-icons/react'

export default function Demo() {
  const [align, setAlign] = useState<'start' | 'center' | 'end'>('start')
  const [snap, setSnap] = useState(true)
  const [mode, setMode] = useState<'normal' | 'multiply' | 'screen'>('normal')
  return (
    <div className="demo-row">
      <Segmented
        label="Alignment"
        value={align}
        onChange={setAlign}
        segments={[
          { value: 'start', icon: TextAlignStartIcon, label: 'Left' },
          { value: 'center', icon: TextAlignCenterIcon, label: 'Center' },
          { value: 'end', icon: TextAlignEndIcon, label: 'Right' },
        ]}
      />
      <BarSeparator />
      <Choice label="Mode" value={mode} onChange={setMode} choices={[['normal', 'Normal'], ['multiply', 'Multiply'], ['screen', 'Screen']]} />
      <Checkbox label="Snap" checked={snap} onChange={setSnap} />
      <Hint>Alt-drag to copy</Hint>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Segmented props

Buttons of which one is pressed: icons (selection modes, alignment) or words (24h, 7d, 30d).

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The group's accessible name (for example "Selection mode"). |
| `value` (required) | `V` |  |  |
| `segments` (required) | `readonly Segment<V>[]` |  |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onChange` (required) | `(value: V) => void` |  |  |
| `testId` | `string` |  | Each button's test id is `${testId}-${value}`. |

### Choice props

A drop-down choice with its label before it.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `quiet` | `boolean` |  | Draws no visible label (the drop-down still has `label` as its name). |
| `value` (required) | `V` |  |  |
| `choices` (required) | `readonly (readonly [V, string])[]` |  |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onChange` (required) | `(value: V) => void` |  |  |
| `testId` | `string` |  |  |

### Checkbox props

A check box with its label.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `label` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `checked` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `onChange` | `(checked: boolean) => void` |  |  |
| `testId` | `string` |  |  |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |

### Hint props

A muted usage hint in a row.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `testId` | `string` |  |  |

### BarSeparator props

A hairline between groups of controls in a row.

## Form

Forms. A form that keeps its values and checks them against rules before onFinish; useForm reaches it from outside, useWatch reads one field.

```ts
import { Form, FormItem } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- A settings page, a create or edit dialog, any form with validation.

When not to:

- One setting that applies at once: use a Switch on its own.

### Example: Rules, help, reset

Submit with the email empty to see the errors; they re-check as you type.

```tsx
import { Button, Checkbox, Form, FormItem, NumberInput, Select, TextInput, toast, useForm, useWatch } from '@kition/tessera'

type Values = { email: string; credits: number | null; reason: string; plan: string; notify: boolean }

export default function Demo() {
  const form = useForm<Values>()
  const credits = useWatch<number>('credits', form)
  return (
    <div style={{ maxWidth: 420 }}>
      <Form<Values> form={form} initialValues={{ email: '', credits: 100, reason: '', plan: 'pro', notify: true }} onFinish={(values) => toast('success', 'Credits added', `${values.credits} credits for ${values.email}`)}>
        <FormItem name="email" label="Email" rules={[{ required: true }, { type: 'email' }]}>
          <TextInput size="md" placeholder="ada@example.com" />
        </FormItem>
        <FormItem name="credits" label="Credits" rules={[{ required: true }, { min: 1, max: 100000 }]} extra={credits ? `About $${(credits / 100).toFixed(2)} of usage.` : undefined}>
          <NumberInput size="md" min={1} step={10} />
        </FormItem>
        <FormItem name="plan" label="Plan">
          <Select size="md">
            <option value="free">Free</option>
            <option value="pro">Pro</option>
            <option value="team">Team</option>
          </Select>
        </FormItem>
        <FormItem name="reason" label="Reason" rules={[{ required: true, whitespace: true }, { max: 120 }]} extra="Recorded in the credit ledger.">
          <TextInput size="md" />
        </FormItem>
        <FormItem name="notify" valuePropName="checked">
          <Checkbox label="Email the person" />
        </FormItem>
        <div style={{ display: 'flex', gap: 8 }}>
          <Button type="submit" variant="primary" size="md">Add credits</Button>
          <Button size="md" onClick={() => form.resetFields()}>Reset</Button>
        </div>
      </Form>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Form props

A form that keeps its fields' values and checks them before `onFinish`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `form` | `FormInstance<T>` |  |  |
| `initialValues` | `Partial<T>` |  | The values it starts with (read once). |
| `onFinish` | `(values: T) => void` |  | Called with the values when the person submits and every field passes. |
| `onValuesChange` | `(changed: Partial<T>, values: T) => void` |  |  |
| `layout` | `FormLayout` | `'vertical'` | `vertical` (default): labels above controls; `inline`: fields in a row (filters). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `id` | `string` |  |  |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |

### FormItem props

A labelled control bound to one field of the form around it, with its rules and error.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` |  | The field's name in the values; without it the item only lays out a label and a control. |
| `label` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `rules` | `readonly FormRule[]` | `[]` |  |
| `extra` | `ReactNode` |  | Help under the control (replaced by the error while there is one). |
| `required` | `boolean` |  | Marks the label as required (implied by a `required` rule). |
| `valuePropName` | `string` | `'value'` | The control's prop that holds the value: `checked` for a check box or switch. |
| `trigger` | `string` | `'onChange'` | The control's prop that reports a change: `onCheckedChange` for a switch. |
| `getValueFromEvent` | `(...args: any[]) => unknown` | `fromEvent` | The value from what the control reports (an event's `target.value` or `checked`, or the value itself, by default). |
| `dependencies` | `readonly string[]` | `[]` | Fields whose changes re-check this one (a confirmation of a password). |
| `hidden` | `boolean` |  | Kept in the values but not drawn. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | One control element. |

## Combobox and MultiSelect

Forms. One choice from a long list, searched as the person types or on the server with onSearch, and several choices toggled in a list.

```ts
import { Combobox, MultiSelect } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- Picking a user, a record, a country: more choices than a Select shows well.

When not to:

- A handful of fixed choices: use Select.

### Example: Search and pick

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Combobox } from '@kition/tessera'

const PEOPLE = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Margaret Hamilton', 'Edsger Dijkstra', 'Barbara Liskov', 'Donald Knuth']

export default function Demo() {
  const [person, setPerson] = useState<number | undefined>(2)
  return (
    <div style={{ maxWidth: 320 }}>
      <Combobox
        label="Person"
        size="md"
        placeholder="Search people"
        value={person}
        onChange={setPerson}
        options={PEOPLE.map((name, index) => ({ value: index + 1, label: index === 5 ? `${name} (no GitHub)` : name, disabled: index === 5 }))}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Example: Several choices

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { MultiSelect } from '@kition/tessera'

const MODES = ['free', 'reward', 'paid', 'hosted'].map((value) => ({ value, label: value }))

export default function Demo() {
  const [modes, setModes] = useState(['paid', 'hosted'])
  return (
    <div style={{ maxWidth: 280 }}>
      <MultiSelect label="Mode" placeholder="Any mode" size="md" values={modes} onChange={setModes} options={MODES} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Combobox props

One choice from a long list, searched as the person types; the choice can be cleared.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` (required) | `V \| undefined` |  |  |
| `onChange` (required) | `(value: V \| undefined) => void` |  |  |
| `options` (required) | `readonly ComboboxOption<V>[]` |  |  |
| `onSearch` | `(query: string) => void` |  | Search on the server: called with each query, and the options shown are the caller's. Without it, the options are filtered here. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  |  |
| `emptyText` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown when nothing matches. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The control's accessible name. |
| `size` | `ControlSize` | `'sm'` |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `testId` | `string` |  |  |

### MultiSelect props

Several choices from a list: the chosen ones in the field, toggled in a list (searchable once it is long).

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `values` (required) | `readonly V[]` |  |  |
| `onChange` (required) | `(values: V[]) => void` |  |  |
| `options` (required) | `readonly ComboboxOption<V>[]` |  |  |
| `placeholder` | `string` |  | Shown when nothing is chosen. |
| `label` (required) | `string` |  | The control's accessible name. |
| `size` | `ControlSize` | `'sm'` |  |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `testId` | `string` |  |  |

## NumberInput, DateTimeInput, Popconfirm

Forms. A number field that is empty as null, a date or date-and-time field, and a confirmation beside the button it guards.

```ts
import { NumberInput, DateTimeInput, Popconfirm } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

### Example: Price, start time, delete

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, DateTimeInput, NumberInput, Popconfirm, toast } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  const [price, setPrice] = useState<number | null>(0.25)
  const [start, setStart] = useState<string | null>('2026-10-25T09:00')
  return (
    <div className="demo-row" style={{ alignItems: 'flex-end' }}>
      <label style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 6 }}>
        Price per call
        <NumberInput value={price} onChange={setPrice} min={0} step={0.05} precision={2} style={{ width: 140 }} />
      </label>
      <label style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 6 }}>
        From
        <DateTimeInput withTime value={start} onChange={setStart} />
      </label>
      <Popconfirm title="Delete this pricing rule?" description="Calls are charged by the default rule afterwards." danger okText="Delete" onConfirm={() => toast('success', 'Rule deleted')}>
        <Button variant="danger">Delete rule</Button>
      </Popconfirm>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### NumberInput props

A field for a number, empty as `null`; arrows step it, and it rounds to `precision` when left.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `number \| null \| ''` |  | Optional inside a `FormItem`, which supplies it. |
| `onChange` | `(value: number \| null) => void` |  |  |
| `min` | `number` |  |  |
| `max` | `number` |  |  |
| `step` | `number` | `1` |  |
| `precision` | `number` |  | Decimals kept when the field is left. |
| `size` | `ControlSize` | `'sm'` |  |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  |  |

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

### DateTimeInput props

A date, or a date and time, from the platform's picker; cleared to `null`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string \| null` |  | Optional inside a `FormItem`, which supplies it. |
| `onChange` | `(value: string \| null) => void` |  |  |
| `withTime` | `boolean` |  | Asks for a time too. |
| `size` | `ControlSize` | `'sm'` |  |
| `invalid` | `boolean` |  |  |

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

### Popconfirm props

Asks "are you sure?" next to the button that does something, before it does.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `onConfirm` (required) | `() => void` |  |  |
| `okText` | `string` |  |  |
| `cancelText` | `string` |  |  |
| `danger` | `boolean` |  | Draws OK as a destructive button. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` |  | Lets the trigger act without asking. |
| `children` (required) | `ReactElement` |  | The button that asks. |

## Table

Data display. Records in rows and columns: columns say what each shows, dataSource holds the records; pages, pinned columns, loading and empty states.

```ts
import { Table, Pagination } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- Lists of orders, users, events: anything scanned and compared row by row.

When not to:

- A spreadsheet the person edits: that is a kit.

### Example: Pages, pinned column, tags

```tsx
import { Table, Tag, type TableColumn } from '@kition/tessera'

type Order = { id: string; customer: string; plan: string; amount: number; status: 'paid' | 'pending' | 'refunded' }

const ORDERS: Order[] = Array.from({ length: 23 }, (_, index) => ({
  id: `ord_${1040 + index}`,
  customer: ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Katherine Johnson'][index % 4],
  plan: index % 3 ? 'Pro' : 'Team',
  amount: 19 + (index % 5) * 10,
  status: (['paid', 'pending', 'refunded'] as const)[index % 3],
}))

const TONES = { paid: 'success', pending: 'warning', refunded: 'neutral' } as const

const columns: TableColumn<Order>[] = [
  { key: 'id', title: 'Order', dataIndex: 'id', width: 120, fixed: 'left' },
  { key: 'customer', title: 'Customer', dataIndex: 'customer', ellipsis: true },
  { key: 'plan', title: 'Plan', dataIndex: 'plan', width: 90 },
  { key: 'amount', title: 'Amount', dataIndex: 'amount', align: 'right', width: 100, render: (amount: number) => `$${amount}.00` },
  { key: 'status', title: 'Status', dataIndex: 'status', width: 110, render: (status: Order['status']) => <Tag tone={TONES[status]}>{status}</Tag> },
]

export default function Demo() {
  return <Table columns={columns} dataSource={ORDERS} rowKey="id" size="small" pagination={{ defaultPageSize: 8, showSizeChanger: true, pageSizeOptions: [8, 16, 32] }} />
}
```

### Example: Empty and loading

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Button, Empty, Table, type TableColumn } from '@kition/tessera'

type Key = { id: string; name: string }
const columns: TableColumn<Key>[] = [
  { key: 'name', title: 'Name', dataIndex: 'name' },
  { key: 'id', title: 'ID', dataIndex: 'id', width: 160 },
]

export default function Demo() {
  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 16 }}>
      <Table columns={columns} dataSource={[]} rowKey="id" emptyText={<Empty title="No API keys" description="Create a key to call the API from your own code."><Button size="sm" variant="primary">Create key</Button></Empty>} />
      <Button size="sm" onClick={() => { setLoading(true); setTimeout(() => setLoading(false), 1500) }}>Load for 1.5s</Button>
      <Table columns={columns} dataSource={[{ id: 'key_1', name: 'Build server' }]} rowKey="id" loading={loading} />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Table props

Records in rows and columns: `columns` say what each shows (`dataIndex`, `render`), `dataSource`
holds the records. Pages through long lists, shows a spinner while loading and `emptyText` when
empty, and can pin columns and the header.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `columns` (required) | `readonly TableColumn<T>[]` |  |  |
| `dataSource` (required) | `readonly T[] \| undefined` |  |  |
| `rowKey` (required) | `string \| ((record: T) => Key)` |  | The field that identifies a record, or a function of it. |
| `loading` | `boolean` |  |  |
| `pagination` | `TablePagination \| false` |  | Pages of `defaultPageSize` rows (10 by default); `false` shows every row. |
| `size` | `'small' \| 'middle'` | `'middle'` | `small`: 36px rows for dense screens; `middle` (default): 44px. |
| `emptyText` | `ReactNode` |  | Shown when there are no rows (an `Empty`). |
| `sticky` | `boolean` |  | Keeps the header in view while the page scrolls. |
| `scrollX` | `number \| string` |  | The table's least width; it scrolls sideways in a narrower container. |
| `onRow` | `(record: T, index: number) => HTMLAttributes<HTMLTableRowElement>` |  |  |
| `caption` | `ReactNode` |  | Caption above the table, for its accessible name. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `testId` | `string` |  |  |

### Pagination props

The pages of a long list: the range shown, page buttons, and an optional page size.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `page` (required) | `number` |  |  |
| `pageSize` (required) | `number` |  |  |
| `total` (required) | `number` |  |  |
| `onChange` (required) | `(page: number, pageSize: number) => void` |  |  |
| `pageSizeOptions` | `readonly number[]` |  | Offers these page sizes; without it the size is fixed. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

## Tag

Data display. A short status or category label on a soft tint of its tone.

```ts
import { Tag } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- A record’s status in a table or header.

When not to:

- A count beside a label: use Badge.

### Example: Tones

```tsx
import { Tag } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  return (
    <div className="demo-row">
      <Tag>Draft</Tag>
      <Tag tone="info">Processing</Tag>
      <Tag tone="success">Paid</Tag>
      <Tag tone="warning">Pending</Tag>
      <Tag tone="danger">Failed</Tag>
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Tag props

A short status or category label on a soft tint of its tone.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `Tone` | `'neutral'` |  |

Also takes the attributes of its HTML element.

## Alert

Data display. A message in the page, in its tone, with an optional action or close.

```ts
import { Alert } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

When to use:

- A state of the account or page the person should know about.

When not to:

- A short confirmation after an action: use a toast.

### Example: Tones, action, close

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react'
import { Alert, Button } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  const [shown, setShown] = useState(true)
  return (
    <div style={{ display: 'grid', gap: 8 }}>
      <Alert title="Password sign-in is turned off" description="People sign in with GitHub or Google until you turn it back on." />
      <Alert tone="success" title="Credits added" />
      <Alert tone="warning" title="Your plan renews in 3 days" action={<Button size="sm">Manage</Button>} />
      {shown ? <Alert tone="danger" title="The last payment failed" description="Update the card to keep syncing." onClose={() => setShown(false)} /> : null}
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Alert props

A message in the page: what happened or what to know, in its tone, with an optional action.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tone` | `Exclude<Tone, 'neutral'>` | `'info'` |  |
| `title` (required) | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `description` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `action` | `ReactNode` |  | A button or link at the end (Retry, Upgrade). |
| `onClose` | `() => void` |  | Shows a close button that calls it. |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |
| `testId` | `string` |  |  |

## Descriptions

Data display. Labelled values of one record, in columns; with Breadcrumb, Avatar, and Divider for a detail page.

```ts
import { Descriptions, Breadcrumb, Avatar, Divider } from '@kition/tessera' // in a kit: '@kition/kit-ui'
```

### Example: A user’s detail page

```tsx
import { Avatar, Breadcrumb, Descriptions, Divider, Tag } from '@kition/tessera'

export default function Demo() {
  return (
    <div>
      <Breadcrumb items={[{ title: <a href="#users">Users</a> }, { title: 'Ada Lovelace' }]} />
      <div style={{ display: 'flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 10, margin: '12px 0' }}>
        <Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" size={36} />
        <strong>Ada Lovelace</strong>
        <Tag tone="success">active</Tag>
      </div>
      <Divider>Account</Divider>
      <Descriptions
        columns={3}
        items={[
          { label: 'Email', children: 'ada@example.com' },
          { label: 'Plan', children: 'Pro (yearly)' },
          { label: 'Credits', children: '12,400' },
          { label: 'Signed up', children: '2026-03-14 09:21' },
          { label: 'Last active', children: '2 hours ago' },
          { label: 'Notes', children: 'Moved from the Team plan after the trial.', span: 3 },
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  )
}
```

### Descriptions props

Labelled values of one record (an order, a user), laid out in `columns` columns.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `readonly DescriptionItem[]` |  |  |
| `columns` | `number` | `3` |  |
| `title` | `ReactNode` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

### Breadcrumb props

Where the page sits: its parents (links in `title`) and then itself.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` (required) | `readonly BreadcrumbItem[]` |  |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

### Avatar props

A person's picture, or their initial on a tint when there is none.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` |  |  |
| `name` (required) | `string` |  |  |
| `size` | `number` | `28` |  |
| `className` | `string` |  |  |

### Divider props

A hairline between sections, with an optional label in it.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
